types.description: PDP22-FBP.025 PROFIBUS DP-V1 FieldBusPlug, integral 0.25 m cable

document.title: PDP21-FBP / PDP22-FBP PROFIBUS DP FieldBusPlugs — Technical Description

modelingNotes: Exact ABB 1SAJ240100R0003 is PDP22-FBP.025, a PROFIBUS DP-V1 FieldBusPlug with 0.25 m integral cable (2004 manual p.30).

External-interface abstraction of the complete factory cable/plug assembly: IN is the passive cable-end plug X13; OUT is the onward PROFIBUS socket; DEV is the fieldbus-neutral device socket. IN/OUT/DEV are authoring aliases. ABB p.27 labels both sockets X12, so they must not share a key. Pin numbers 1-5 are manufacturer identities; no separately accessible cable clamps are documented.

Bus pins: 1 +24 V DC/brown, 2 Bus-N=A/green, 3 0 V DC/blue, 4 red bus conductor, 5 shield/bare. Historical pp.27/29 call pin 4 Bus-B=A, but p.27 lower diagram says Signal P/B. The 07.2006 manual p.28 says Bus-P=B. Preserve pin 4 as the red bus conductor without resolving this inconsistent A/B text into an installation instruction.

DEV pins: 1 +24 V; 3 0 V; parallel mode 2 DI1, 4 DI0, 5 DO0; serial mode 2 diagnosis, 4 and 5 serial data. Modes share physical pins. Singleton bus functions render endpoints only, without simulating active conversion, mode selection, signal direction or protocol behavior. PROFIBUS is not Ethernet; no logical Ethernet ports are authored.

Factory continuity requires explicit fixture jumpers IN.1-OUT.1 through IN.5-OUT.5 (passive tee and integral cable, manual pp.9-12,27,29); also IN.1-DEV.1 and IN.3-DEV.3 (explicit internal potential diagram p.27). Metadata never joins nets. DEV.2/4/5 remain separate from bus data and each other. No shield-to-0V or shield-to-PE jumper is asserted. The downstream termination unit and device INT/EXT switch are separate equipment.

Bus supply 24 V DC +30%/-20% (19.2-31.2 V DC). Consumption 46 mA at 19.2 V, 37 mA at 24 V, 31 mA at 31.2 V; total dissipation max.0.9 W. Plug/cable load max.4 A; supply to a connected device should not exceed 200 mA (pp.16,29). These conditional ratings are notes, not scalar terminal current or assigned circuit voltage.

IP65 with M12 box-nut device fixing; IP20 with supplied fastening screw. Operating ambient 0 to +55 degC (p.29). Shield grounding is an installation connection (pp.19-20), not an automatic bond through mounting hardware. Shell-to-shield and device-side metalwork continuity are not exhaustively documented.

Only IN.1 and IN.3 are required, representing the universally needed bus supply/return nets (p.16); fixed links can satisfy presence but do not prove external power. Shared policy permits explicit factory-link representation plus external wiring, not multiple conductors in a socket. Device signals and onward use are application-dependent.

connectionCoverage.notes: All 15 numbered contacts across integral passive plug, onward bus socket and neutral device socket are inventoried. IN/OUT/DEV disambiguate duplicate X12 socket labels. Factory bus and supply continuity is specified separately. Shell-to-shield and device-side metalwork bonding are not exhaustively documented; no additional PE terminal is invented. Bus pin 4 textual A/B labeling is inconsistent in the historical manual; numerical identity and red conductor are retained.
